The '''''Annals of Mathematical Statistics''''' was a peer-reviewed statistics [[Academic journal|journal]] published by the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] from 1930 to 1972. It was superseded by the ''[[Annals of Statistics]]'' and the ''[[Annals of Probability]]''.  In 1938, [[Samuel S. Wilks|Samuel Wilks]] became editor-in-chief of the ''Annals'' and recruited a remarkable editorial staff: [[Ronald Fisher|Fisher]], [[Jerzy Neyman|Neyman]], [[Harald Cramér|Cramér]], [[Harold Hotelling|Hotelling]], [[Egon Pearson]], [[Georges Darmois]], Allen T. Craig, [[W. Edwards Deming|Deming]], [[Richard von Mises|von Mises]], [[H. L. Rietz]], and [[Walter A. Shewhart|Shewhart]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://imstat.org/history.htm |title=History of the Founding of the IMS — Institute for Mathematical Statistics |access-date=2013-02-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131030084159/http://www.imstat.org/history.htm |archive-date=2013-10-30 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
